description: Single-lane sequencer holding four sixteen-step phrases that cross over and mutate as they play, with two optional built-in quantizers

params.text: Starts and stops the sequencer; starting it generates a fresh random walk and derives all four phrases from it, and stopping it returns to the first step and clears the envelope
Sets how many steps a phrase plays before wrapping, 2 to 16; the number under the knob is the current setting
Each press moves to the next mutation engine and the lamp shows which is in force, Gaussian to Markov to Interval and round again; the maker's tooltip also offers AI, which this build does not have
Sets the attack time of the note envelope, 0 to 4 seconds; at 0 the envelope jumps straight to 10V
Sets the decay time of the note envelope, 0 to 4 seconds measured from 10V down to 0V
Brings that phrase into the playing cycle or drops it out; switching it on re-seeds the phrase from the shared random walk, and the lamp pulses while that phrase is the one playing
Sets how far that phrase mutates each round, how likely it is to keep the result, and how many rests and ties it carries; fully left is close to frozen and fully right drifts hardest

inputs.text: Advances the sequence by one step on each rising edge above 1V; there is no internal clock, so the sequence moves only while pulses arrive here
Pulls each newly generated pitch a fifth of the way toward the voltage here, one volt per octave, typically taken from another instance's 1v/O output; with nothing patched no pull is applied

outputs.text: The current note as a pitch, between 0V and 5V, quantized to whichever scale governs the playing phrase and held until the next note; it is 0V while the sequencer is stopped
The note envelope, rising to 10V over the Rise time and falling over the Fall time, with a tied step freezing the fall so the note carries on, despite the panel printing Gate

notes: nothing plays until three things are done: press Run, patch a clock into Clock, and switch at least one phrase's toggle on.
the quantizers are optional. The left one governs phrases 1 and 3 and the right one phrases 2 and 4, but where only one side has any note switched on, that side governs all four.
with every note switched off on both quantizers the pitch output is not quantized at all, and carries the raw generated voltages.
a new note fires only once the previous envelope has finished, so a Rise and Fall that together outlast the gap between clock pulses leave some steps silent.
the step count and the changes of phrase are driven by the clock alone, and run at the same rate whether or not a step was audible.
each phrase that is switched on plays four passes of the sequence before the next one takes over, and once every switched-on phrase has had its turn they all evolve.
a phrase that has drifted from its starting version has a one in four chance, each time its turn comes round, of playing that original version for one pass instead.
the Recall lamp is lit while a phrase is playing its original version rather than its evolved one.
the Drift lamp flashes at the start of a phrase's turn when that phrase's content changed since it last played, and fades over about 7 seconds.
generated pitches are pulled back toward 2.5V and pushed by whole octaves back inside 1.25V to 3.75V, so the melody stays within about two and a half octaves.

inputs.0:
high above 1V · stepped · one channel only

unpatched it reads 0V; a negative voltage does nothing here.
inputs.1:
1V per octave · continuous · one channel only

unpatched it reads no pull applied; a negative voltage subtracts from the knob.
